PURPOSE: To determine the Km and Kcat of enzymes.

DATA: Enter substrate concentration into X, and enzyme velocity into Y. Use different oolumns for different experimental conditions.

CONSTANTS: You must constrain Et to a constant value, based on other experiments. Et is the concentration of enzyme catalytic sites. PARAMETERS:  
kcat: Turnover number -- number of times each enzyme site converts substrate to product per unit time (expressed in inverse of the time units of the Y axis).

Km is the Michaelis-Menten constant, in the same units as X. It is the substrate concentration needed to get a half-maximum enzyme velocity.

ASSUMPTIONS: 1. All substrate production is due to enzyme activity. 2. The enzyme is at "steady state" which means the that substrate production is linear with time (this means you don't measure activity too soon or too late).

NOTES: This model fits exactly the same curve as the standard Micheaelis-Menten equation that determines Km and Vmax. The difference is that this equation fits Et rather than Vmax. The product of Kcat times Et is the Vmax (in the same units as Y).

DATA: Enter substrate concentration into X, and enzyme velocity into Y. Use different oolumns for different experimental conditions.

model_catalog.source_name: Continuous hinge function. Segmental regression lines with gentle connection
model_catalog.source_description:
This is similar to segmental regression, except that the change between the two lines is gentle. 

Intercept: Y at X=0
Slope1:  Slope when X<X0
Slope2: Slope when X>X0
Delta: Defines how sharp the bend is. When delta is close to zero, the result is is very close to two intersecting lines (segmental regression). As Delta is made larger, the curve joinging the two lines is more spread out. Delta must always be positive.

This hinge function was derived by Andrew Gelman:

http://andrewgelman.com/2017/05/19/continuous-hinge-function-bayesian-modeling/
model_catalog.source_notes: You will usually want to set X0 to a constant value, often the time you changed conditions. You will always want to set (not fit) Delta. It determines how gentle the curve is that connects the two curves.
